entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Phased implementation of ICH M11: Clinical electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP) – Notice to stakeholders
entries.description: This new guideline provides comprehensive clinical protocol organization with standardized content, with a Template which presents the format and structure of the protocol, including the table of contents, common headers, and contents; and a Technical Specification which presents the conformance, cardinality, and other technical attributes that enable the interoperable electronic exchange of protocol content.
entries.summary: The ICH M11 guideline CeSHarP is introduced in a phased manner to standardize clinical protocol structure and enable interoperable electronic exchange.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must incorporate the new structured protocol template and technical specifications to ensure compliance and facilitate digital interoperability.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice to stakeholders on implementing ICH M13B: Bioequivalence for immediate release solid oral dosage forms: Additional strengths biowaiver
entries.description: Part of the foreseen ICH M13 Guideline series (M13A-C), the ICH M13B Guideline is intended to provide recommendations on obtaining waivers of bioequivalence (BE) studies for one or more additional strengths of a drug product in an application where in vivo BE has been demonstrated for at least one of the strengths. This guideline is applicable to both development and post approval phases for orally administered immediate-release (IR) solid oral dosage forms designed to deliver drugs to the systemic circulation, such as tablets, capsules, and granules/powders for oral suspension. The ICH M13B Guideline is the second Guideline in the foreseen series to describe the scientific and technical aspects of demonstrating BE for additional strengths of a drug product, i.e., obtaining waiver(s) for one or more strengths in an application with multiple strengths when BE has been demonstrated for at least one of the strengths following ICH M13A. How regulatory decisions may be made based on BE assessment is out of the scope of this guideline.
entries.summary: ICH M13B guidance provides recommendations for obtaining biowaivers for additional strengths of immediate‑release solid oral dosage forms when BE has been demonstrated for at least one strength.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams developing or approving multi‑strength oral solids must review this guideline to determine if a biowaiver can replace in‑vivo studies for extra strengths, potentially reducing development time and cost.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: ICH guidelines implemented by Health Canada
entries.description: Health Canada has implemented and launched public consultations on several International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines, reflecting Canada’s ongoing commitment to global regulatory harmonization. Stakeholders are encouraged to review and provide feedback on the draft guidelines for consultation by the respective deadlines, as Health Canada will forward all comments to the ICH for consideration in the finalization process. Health Canada has begun implementing finalized guidelines. Stakeholders are encouraged to integrate these guidelines into their drug registration processes.
entries.summary: Health Canada has launched public consultations on several ICH guidelines and is implementing finalized guidelines.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review the draft ICH guidelines, provide feedback before the consultation deadline, and integrate finalized guidelines into their drug registration processes.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Qualifying notice for Calquence (302879)
entries.description: A Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) is authorization to market a drug (i.e. a Notice of Compliance (NOC)), with the condition that the Sponsor undertake additional studies to verify the clinical benefit. Health Canada issues the NOC under section C.08.004 of the Food and Drug Regulations for a submission that qualifies under the Guidance Document: Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c).
entries.summary: Health Canada granted a Notice of Compliance with Conditions for Calquence, requiring additional studies to confirm clinical benefit.
entries.why_it_matters: The RA team must ensure the sponsor completes the mandated studies and complies with the conditions to maintain market authorization.

entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams for cellular and gene therapies must incorporate these potency standards into their development and quality plans to ensure compliance.
